sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match the columns or one word).

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) The Sardhana church was constructed by Begum Samru. (b) Guru Teg Bahadur was the tenth guru of the Sikhs.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: he was the ninth Guru; Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth.

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) Islam was brought to India by the Turks. (b) Prophet Muhammad migrated from Mecca to Medina in 622 AD.
questions.answer: (a) False: it was brought first by Arab merchants. (b) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) In 610 AD, at the age of forty, Hazrat Mohammad got ________. (b) The Dargah of Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki is in the village Mehrauli in ________.
questions.answer: (a) Prophethood. (b) Delhi.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The Prophet got Prophethood at the age of ________ in the year 610 AD. (b) The Hijri era started in the year ________.
questions.answer: (a) Forty. (b) 622 AD.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The word Khalsa means ________. (b) Islam was established in the year ________ at Mecca (as given in the lesson).
questions.answer: (a) The pure. (b) 570 CE.

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) Jesus Christ lived in the region of Palestine. (b) The Christian temple is called a 'Synagogue'.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: it is called a church.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) 'Sikh' comes from the Sanskrit word ________. (b) Guru Nanak's hymns were compiled in the ________.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Write a short note on Hazratbal as a holy place of Muslims.
questions.answer: Hazratbal stands on the bank of the Dal Lake in Srinagar and is the only bulbous-domed mosque in Kashmir. It is sacred because it keeps the sacred hair of the Prophet Muhammad.

or.q: Write a short note on a church as a holy place of Christians (Basilica of Bom Jesus).
or.answer: It is at Old Goa, built in 1605, a World Heritage monument. It holds the relics of St Francis Xavier and an exposition is held every ten years.

questions.q: Describe any two characteristics of Gurudwara Paonta Sahib as a holy place of Sikhs.
questions.answer: It is in Sirmour, Himachal Pradesh, dedicated to Guru Gobind Singh. The name 'Paonta' means 'feet' and it draws devotees in huge numbers.

questions.q: Describe the concept of langar.
questions.answer: A langar is the free kitchen of a gurudwara. People of all castes sit together in pangat to eat, which teaches equality.

questions.q: Describe the five Ks of Sikhs.
questions.answer: They are kesh (uncut hair), kangha (comb), kada (iron bracelet), kachcha (underwear) and kirpan (sword). They were established by Guru Gobind Singh when he founded the Khalsa.

questions.q: How did Christianity come to India? Explain in two points.
questions.answer: St Thomas, a disciple of Jesus, is believed to have reached Muziris on the western coast and founded churches. The Portuguese later brought missionaries such as Francis Xavier to the western coast.

questions.q: What is a dargah? Why is it a tourist attraction?
questions.answer: A dargah is a Sufi shrine built over the grave of a saint, often with a khanqah. It attracts people of all religions, especially on the Urs, with qawwali and fairs.

questions.q: List the major festivals of Muslims.
questions.answer: Eid-ul-Fitr, Eid-ul-Zuha (Bakrid), Moharram and Eid Milad-un-Nabi.

questions.q: Explain 'Takht' in Sikhism.
questions.answer: A takht is the seat of divine power and of social and political decisions of the Gurus. There are five: Akal Takht, Keshgarh, Damdama, Hazur Sahib and Patna Sahib.

questions.q: Who was Begum Samru? Why is Sardhana famous?
questions.answer: Begum Samru was the Roman Catholic wife of a German mercenary, who commanded his force after his death. She built the beautiful Sardhana church near Meerut, a heritage site visited in March and November.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain any three Christian heritage sites located in Tamil Nadu.
questions.answer: (i) St Thomas Mount near Chennai, where St Thomas is believed to have been killed, with a stone cross carved by him. (ii) San Thomas Basilica at Santhome, Chennai, a 16th-century church with stained glass and a statue of Virgin Mary. (iii) The Velankanni church, the most visited pilgrimage centre of Christians in Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: Explain the life of Guru Nanak after 1496 (three points).
questions.answer: (i) In 1496 he had an extraordinary spiritual experience. (ii) With Mardana and Bhai Bala he travelled from village to village preaching love and brotherhood through kirtans and ragas. (iii) He spent his last years at Kartarpur and chose Angad as his successor.

questions.q: Describe the teachings of Guru Nanak in three points.
questions.answer: (i) There is one formless God. (ii) The caste system, idolatry and superstitions should be rejected. (iii) Humility, charity, forgiveness and truthfulness should be practised.

questions.q: Describe the main features of Islamic culture (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Islam is monotheistic and its five pillars are faith, prayer, zakat, fasting and Hajj. (ii) Muslims pray five times a day facing Mecca. (iii) Sufis preached peace and brotherhood and their dargahs and Urs attract all communities.

questions.q: Explain the importance of the Golden Temple (three points).
questions.answer: (i) The town of Amritsar was founded by Guru Ram Das in 1577 on land gifted by Akbar. (ii) Guru Arjan Dev completed the temple and Maharaja Ranjit Singh covered it with gold, so it is the Swarna Mandir. (iii) It is the most sacred shrine of the Sikhs.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Write an essay on the life and teachings of Guru Nanak, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) He was born at Talwandi near Lahore in 1469, the first Guru and a great Bhakti saint. (ii) He learned Sanskrit and Persian and had a spiritual experience in 1496. (iii) With Mardana and Bhai Bala he travelled to spread love and brotherhood through kirtans. (iv) He taught one formless God and rejected caste, idolatry and superstition. (v) He taught humility, charity, forgiveness and truthfulness and began sangat and langar. (vi) His hymns were compiled in the Adi Granth and he chose Angad as successor before dying at Kartarpur (1539).

questions.q: Describe the most popular Sikh Takhts and Gurudwaras in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Sri Akal Takht, founded by Guru Hargobind. (ii) Keshgarh Sahib, where the Khalsa began, and Damdama Sahib, where Guru Gobind Singh completed the Guru Granth Sahib. (iii) Hazur Sahib at Nanded and Patna Sahib on the Ganga. (iv) The Golden Temple at Amritsar and Bangla Sahib in Delhi. (v) Sis Ganj Sahib, where Guru Tegh Bahadur was martyred in 1675. (vi) Hemkund Sahib at 15,200 ft and Paonta Sahib.

questions.q: Describe the most popular Islamic heritage sites available to tourists in India, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki's dargah at Mehrauli with the Phoolwalon ki Sair. (ii) Nizamuddin dargah in Delhi with qawwalis. (iii) Moinuddin Chishti's dargah at Ajmer with its annual Urs. (iv) Hazratbal and Charar-i-Sharif in Kashmir. (v) Haji Ali in Mumbai and Gesu Daraz at Gulbarga. (vi) Nagore dargah in Tamil Nadu with a golden dome and five minarets.

questions.q: Describe five important Christian heritage sites in India, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Basilica of Bom Jesus (Old Goa), with St Francis Xavier's relics. (ii) St Thomas Mount and San Thomas Basilica in Chennai. (iii) Velankanni church in Tamil Nadu. (iv) Thomas Church at Kodungallur in Kerala. (v) Skinner's church in Delhi, the Holy Christ Church in Shimla and the Sardhana church. (vi) The Presbyterian church at Ross Island and Solomon's Temple at Aizawl.
